title: 'Appan Chale Punjab Medal Lai Ke': Baljeet Kaur's Video Goes Viral After Hockey Gold
excerpt: The India hockey star's Punjabi message to fans after the team's 1-0 Asian Games final win over China became an internet favourite.
body:
• Indian hockey star Baljeet Kaur's celebratory video after the Asian Games gold — declaring in Punjabi, "Appan chale Punjab medal lai ke" — has gone viral on social media.
  • India's women beat China 1-0 in the Nagoya final, ending a 44-year wait for Asian Games hockey gold and securing direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
  • Lalremsiami scored the winner in the 10th minute on her 200th senior appearance, while goalkeeper Savita Punia saved a 24th-minute penalty stroke.
  • Baljeet, who made her 50th senior appearance during the tournament and scored in the 19-0 opener against Uzbekistan, was among the defenders who held firm in a tense final.

A celebratory video by Indian hockey star Baljeet Kaur has gone viral after India's women's team beat China 1-0 to win the Asian Games gold in Nagoya. In the clip, Kaur declares in Punjabi, "Appan chale Punjab medal lai ke" — "we're headed to Punjab, taking the medal" — a line that struck a chord with fans and quickly racked up shares across social media, including admiring Punjabi-diaspora posts calling her the "gold medal jittan wali bibi" — the girl who won the gold medal.

The video captured the mood of a triumph that ended 44 years of waiting. India's previous and only Asian Games women's hockey gold had come in 1982; the team reached the final in 1998 and 2018 but finished with silver both times.

"Appan chale Punjab medal lai ke."

— Baljeet Kaur, in a viral video, as reported by The Tribune

Context & Background

The final was decided early. Lalremsiami scored the decisive goal in the 10th minute, marking her 200th senior appearance for India in memorable fashion, turning inside the circle before unleashing a powerful reverse-stick strike into the upper part of the net off an assist from Sakshi Rana.

China hit back quickly, earning a penalty stroke in the 24th minute after Lalremsiami was penalised for obstructing a Chinese forward. Bichu Devi Kharibam had started in goal, but experienced goalkeeper Savita Punia was brought on for the crucial penalty — and dived to her left to make a superb save, denying China their clearest opportunity of the match.

India went into half-time with the 1-0 advantage intact, then defended it through a tense second half as China dominated possession and repeatedly earned penalty corners. Ishika Chaudhary, Baljeet Kaur and Sushila Chanu made crucial interventions, while captain Salima Tete contributed defensively despite briefly leaving the field with an injury. With around five minutes remaining, China removed their goalkeeper for an extra outfield player — but India's defence stayed organised, cleared the ball repeatedly, and the equaliser never came.

Impact & Analysis

Beyond ending the 44-year wait, the 1-0 victory secured direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics — a prize the players valued as much as the medal itself. "LA qualification mattered more than the 44-year wait for Asian Games gold," veteran goalkeeper Savita said after the triumph.

It was also a personal tournament to remember for Baljeet Kaur, who brought up her 50th senior international cap during the Games and scored in India's dominant 19-0 Pool B opener against Uzbekistan at Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium. Her viral moment after the final — pure, unfiltered joy in Punjabi — became the tournament's most-shared Indian celebration outside the official highlights.

The triumph capped a golden stretch for Indian hockey at the Games: the men's team also won gold, beating Malaysia in their final, for what reports called a "golden double."

Diaspora Angle

Kaur's video resonated far beyond Nagoya because of the language she chose. Punjabi hockey fans — from Jalandhar to Toronto to Vancouver — claimed the moment as their own, sharing the clip with pride and turning a post-match celebration into a statement of cultural identity. Few sports are as woven into Punjab's identity as hockey, and a Punjabi star bringing an Asian Games gold home with those words felt, to many fans, like the medal was theirs too.

What's Next

India's women now turn to homecoming celebrations and then to preparation for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, for which they have already booked their ticket. The squad's blend of veterans like Savita and rising stars suggests the Nagoya gold may be the start of a sustained run rather than a one-off — and Baljeet Kaur, at the heart of both the defence and the celebrations, will be central to it.
